Wall of text -

The main things you want to have are gun screwdrivers or screwdriver tips. Gun screwdrivers have parallel vs. tapered blades so more of the tip can get into the screw. This helps keep it from slipping out and damaging the finish. The other thing you want is a brass punch for drifting sights if your gun has a dovetail windage adjust sight. You literally tap it with a hammer to move it over. If your gun uses roll pins, roll pin punches are useful but a straight punch can be used too. The difference is the ball tip on the roll pin punch that locates in the center of the pin. It keeps it there while hammering it out. However, a straight punch (no ball) will do the same thing if sized correctly. You just lightly tap until the pin is going into the hole. Once it is in, the punch stays in place. You need a set of straight punches as many guns have regular pins. Roll pin punches only work on roll pins though. You can get soft-faced hammers anywhere. The gun one they sell is quite small and I would get a larger one so you can use the mass to your advantage. The bench block is nice but expensive. You can make an excellent substitute with a piece of 1/2" aluminum plate or hard plastic like Corian from a kitchen counter. Drill the hole or cut the slot you need as you need it. Lastly, a small container to put parts in as you are working. I use cheap leftover containers.

TL;DR, the master gunsmith set contains a pile of stuff you will rarely use. By what you need for the guns you have or use substitutes.
